heard: Scientists once feared the moon was covered in bottomless, killer quicksand. In the 1960s, Cornell astronomer Thomas Gold warned that lunar dust was deep enough to swallow any spacecraft. To solve the mystery, NASA launched the Surveyor Program to touch the surface before humans did. In June 1966, Surveyor One touched down on firm basaltic rock, proving the bottomless quicksand was a total myth. But when the sun set, robotic cameras caught a ghostly glow hovering over the horizon. Solar radiation strips electrons from the soil, creating electrostatic charges that launch dust kilometers into the sky. Apollo 17 astronauts even sketched these towering rays of levitating glass shards during their final mission. This electrifying fountain proves the moon isn't actually covered in bottomless, killer quicksand. You
